html:
An attempt in 1787 by Hope and Company, the leading bank of Amsterdam, to buy up most of Europe's stock of cochineal so it could push up the price. It failed.

Cochineal is a red dye made from dried insects that live on cactus. It came almost wholly from New Spain, above all Oaxaca in Mexico, and was shipped through Spain. It was one of the most valuable goods from Spanish America after silver, and textile makers across Europe needed it for scarlet cloth.

Hope bought large amounts in Amsterdam and other ports, betting that control of the supply would let it set the price. But more cochineal came onto the market than expected and buyers held back, so the price did not rise as planned and the bank had to sell at a loss.

The historian Fernand Braudel tells the story as an example of what he saw as the real nature of capitalism: big merchants seeking a monopoly, not open competition. It came near the end of Amsterdam's long reign as Europe's market.
sum: An attempt in 1787 by Hope and Company, the leading bank of Amsterdam, to buy up most of Europe's stock of cochineal so it could push up the price. It failed.
